title: Microsoft May Abandon its Clean Energy Powered Data Centre Targets
source_used: TechCrunch, 6 May 2026 (relaying Bloomberg); EnergyNow page returned 403
key_facts: Bloomberg reported that Microsoft is having internal discussions about delaying or scaling back its hourly clean energy matching goal.
Microsoft has said that by 2030 it intends to match 100 percent of its hourly energy use with clean power on the same grid.
Microsoft has made no public announcement and declined to comment on the internal debate.
A Microsoft spokesperson told TechCrunch the company continues to look for opportunities to maintain its annual matching goal.
Annual matching is more lenient than hourly matching: a company can buy more solar power than it uses at midday and still claim it.
In April 2026 Microsoft said it was working with Chevron and Engine No. 1 on a natural gas power plant in West Texas that could eventually generate up to 5 GW.
quote_evidence: Microsoft has yet to make any public announcements, but according to Bloomberg the company is having internal discussions over its hourly clean energy matching goal.
why_it_matters_hint: A big buyer of data centre power may loosen its strictest clean-power pledge as AI building strains it, which affects how clean the new demand is.
notes: OLD NEWS RE-DATED: EnergyNow URL carries /2026/05/; Bloomberg and Reuters reported it on 6 May 2026 and EnergyNow re-published it on 11 Oct 2026. A search of the last 45 days found no Microsoft decision. EnergyNow's headline says data-centre targets; the pledge covers Microsoft's hourly energy use generally. Bloomberg page not opened; its link was decoded from Google News.
